questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=1 \\  & 2x+3y+4z=6 \\  & 3x+3y+4z=11\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & 4 & 11\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & 4 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & 3 & 4 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=1 \\  & y=4 \\  & z=-4\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. Substituting both $y=4$ and $z=-4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(4)+2(-4)=1\,⟹\,x=5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=5,y=4$, and $z=-4.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨5,4,-4⟩.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y+z=-4 \\  & 2x+5y+3z=-10 \\  & 3x+6y+4z=-12\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 & -10 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 & -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 & -10 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $-\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{7}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{7}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=1 \\  & y-3z=-9 \\  & z=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y-3(1)=-9\,⟹\,y=-6.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-6$ and $z=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x-(-6)+2(1)=1\,⟹\,x=-7.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-7,y=-6$, and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-7,-6,1⟩.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=1 \\ y-z=-4 \\ z=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(1)=-4\,⟹\,y=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3(-3)=1\,⟹\,x=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-8$, $y=-3$, and $z=1.$
